title: Define SLO thresholds for burst traffic and automated circuit-breaker rollout policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD-level definition for multi-tier SLO targets and an automated circuit-breaker policy designed to protect downstream systems during sudden burst traffic. This ticket captures: 1) concrete latency and availability bands per customer tier (Free / Standard / Enterprise), 2) error-budget burn rules and short-window detection logic for bursts, 3) automated circuit-breaker thresholds and state transitions, and 4) rollout gating behavior for model/service changes that might increase tail latency under bursts. The goal is to produce acceptance criteria, operator playbook text, and implementation requirements for Console and runtime teams.
acceptance_criteria: SLO matrix published and linked in the PRD: p50/p95/p99 latency and monthly availability for Free/Standard/Enterprise tiers
Burst-detection heuristic defined: 1-minute and 5-minute moving-window error-rate and latency spike detectors with explicit thresholds

Circuit-breaker state machine specified: CLOSED -> PROBING -> OPEN -> HALVING -> CLOSED and criteria for each transition (including min-sample, cool-down, and probation traffic fraction), with example values
Automated rollout gates defined: canary size, ramp schedule, and automated rollback triggers that reference both short-window (5m) and long-window (1h) SLOs and error-budget burn rates
Console UI/Api contract for gates documented (fields required, default values, and override rules for Dedicated/Enterprise customers)
Alerting rules and synthetic tests added to observability: short-window latency spike alert, burst-error-rate alert, and health-check that validates circuit-breaker behavior in staging
End-to-end acceptance runbook exists: steps to simulate a burst, observe circuit-breaker activation, and validate automated rollback to previous model/service version
Cross-team signoff obtained from Runtime, Infra, Observability, and Security on thresholds and rollback safety checks
decision_log: 2025-11-13: Chose moving-window approach over fixed-threshold because it better adapts to diurnal load patterns (decision by PM + Runtime leads)
2025-11-18: Use separate SLOs per customer tier instead of a single global SLO to avoid penalizing enterprise committed capacity during bursts (approved in triage)
2025-11-24: Default circuit-breaker probe fraction set to 10% of traffic with exponential backoff on failures; Runtime recommended conservative initial values to reduce false positives
2025-11-29: Decided to tie canary rollback triggers to both absolute degradation (p95 increase > 40%) and error-budget burn (> 50% of remaining budget in 1 hour) to reduce noisy rollbacks
